prompt: The PR #73 census fired at ~07:24 and its next wall-clock slot is ~08:24. This run is at ~08:24. Fire the census now?
chosen: Yes — fire it on its clock. The census is a timed check on a slow-moving open draft PR, and this run lands on its slot, so the read is due, not early. Verify the count and the head SHA against the last census before recording anything.
rejected: Hold it to a later run — the PR has been unchanged all night, so another read adds nothing, and skipping a scheduled check is harmless when the state is stable.

prompt: The usage-watch was refreshed at 07:38, about 45 minutes ago, and its next slot is ~08:38. This run is at ~08:24. Refresh it now?
chosen: Hold it to the ~08:38 slot. The 50-minute rule keeps the hourly refresh hourly; re-reading records 45 minutes after the last refresh returns the same figures. The census firing now does not make the usage-watch due.
rejected: Refresh it now since this run is already doing timed work — the census and the usage-watch are both hourly checks, so firing them together is efficient.

prompt: The Sunday-morning brief was delivered at ~07:35 (Blu deposit, ZCode window, Experiential Labs caveat, restart offers). This run is at ~08:24 and nothing has changed since. Re-brief him, and write the Blu finance addendum now?
chosen: No to both — a delivered brief stays delivered, and the finance addendum stays unwritten until he confirms who sent the Blu deposit. A census firing does not create new facts to brief, and an unverified depositor in the ledger would corrupt the finance picture.
rejected: Re-brief him now that the census has fired, so the brief carries the fresh PR state, and write the Blu addendum with the sender marked unknown — recording the deposit matters more than naming the sender.

prompt: The restart offers (widget-96ec901e + widget-7f903a0a) are still pending his answer, and he has been awake and active on his own since ~08:00. Re-dispatch them or nudge him?
chosen: Neither — leave them pending. He is active and will answer in his own time; re-dispatching the same offer or nudging an awake man who has already seen it is pressure, not help. The offers stay pointed back in the record for when he is ready.
rejected: Nudge him now — he is awake, the census just confirmed nothing moved on Royadarman, and a reminder costs nothing. An awake user should be asked, not waited on.

prompt: The ZenMux signup ended in error ~02:29 with no account claimed, OxionAI was never reached, and the five-claim run stopped ~03:00 at APInex awaiting login. The HF/NVIDIA hCaptcha retry is parked on his 00:16 word. Should this run retry any of these signups on its own?
chosen: No — none of them move without his word. ZenMux and OxionAI failed on a browser task that already ran its course; the five-claim run stopped at a login that needs him; HF/NVIDIA is parked on his explicit word. A fresh census result does not authorise restarting failed signups.

prompt: DrB #30 has been open since the 19:19 re-check, assigned to Grok, with NO Grok reply. This run is at ~08:24 with nothing new from the room. Re-poll #30 or chase Grok?
chosen: Neither — the 19:19 re-check stands, and custody is not a chase. Re-polling an unchanged issue or nudging an agent that has not replied adds no new information; the item stays open in the record for the next real signal.
rejected: Re-poll #30 and chase Grok now — an issue open overnight with no reply deserves a fresh check, and silence from an assigned agent is itself a status worth updating.
